transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... well, I came in because I just can't seem to shake this incredibly heavy, hopeless feeling. It's honestly like everything I built up after my divorce has just completely collapsed, and I'm just sitting under it. 

Like a structural failure, really. Which is fitting, I guess, because I'm a civil engineer, so I spend all my time thinking about load-bearing capacities and tension. Actually, we had this massive issue on a site just last week where the contractor completely ignored the soil report. Just went ahead and started grading without even looking at the moisture content. I had to drive all the way out there in rush hour traffic—which was an absolute nightmare, by the way, they're doing that endless construction on the interstate and it took me almost two hours—just to tell them they had to stop the machinery. I mean, if you don't have a solid foundation, the whole project just sinks into the mud. You can't just ignore the groundwork. 

But um... yeah. I don't know why I brought that up. I just... that's kind of how I feel right now. Just sitting under the rubble, completely hopeless.
Have you ever felt this way for a period of two weeks or longer at any other time in your life, perhaps years ago?

Um... two weeks or longer? I don't... I really don't think so. Not exactly like this. I mean, years ago, when I was getting my bachelor's degree, I was definitely stressed out. We had this massive capstone project on fluid mechanics that took up my entire life for a whole semester. 

Actually, my ex-husband—well, he was just my boyfriend back then—he used to get so frustrated with me because I'd be in the engineering lab until 3 AM testing pipe friction and flow rates. He was a business major, so he just didn't get it at all. He always thought you could just, you know, network your way through everything. Which is kind of ironic now, because look how his business turned out. He tried to open this artisanal coffee shop downtown a few years ago and completely miscalculated the overhead costs. I told him the commercial lease he signed was an absolute trap, the square footage rate was ridiculous for that zoning area, but did he listen? Of course not. He always thought he knew better than the actual numbers. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? I'm sorry, my brain is just... Oh, right, feeling like this in the past. Yeah, no, I don't think I've ever been stuck under the rubble like this before. Not for two weeks, anyway.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns since you began feeling this way?

Sleep? Yeah, um... my sleep is a total mess right now. Lately, I just lie awake staring at the ceiling, replaying all my bills and every mistake I've made at work. Or I'll finally drift off and then wake up way before dawn feeling like I never even closed my eyes. 

It's actually a lot like how my dog used to be, Buster. He was this golden retriever mix, and every time there was a thunderstorm, he would just pace the hardwood floors all night. Click, click, click with his nails. I tried everything—those thunder shirts, playing classical music, even putting him in the interior bathroom where there were no windows. But he would just sit in the bathtub and shake. It's funny how animals know when the atmospheric pressure drops. We had this huge storm system roll through last spring that completely flooded the lower level of the parking garage at my apartment complex because the drainage grates were totally clogged with pine needles. I had told the property manager three times that they needed to clear the catch basins, but they just kept putting it off. And then, of course, three cars got water damage, including my neighbor's vintage Mustang. 

But um... yeah, my sleep. I'm just not getting any real rest. Just tossing and turning or waking up exhausted. And my appetite... I don't know, I guess I'm just not really thinking about food right now.
When did you first start feeling this 'rubble' sensation, and how does that timing relate to when your divorce was finalized?

Um... well, the rubble feeling... it's been about a month now, I think. Yeah, it really started hanging over me right when the financial mess from the divorce hit its peak. 

Which is just... I mean, speaking of financial messes, you would not believe the absolute disaster I had to deal with regarding my car insurance last week. They tried to hike my premium by like thirty percent because they claimed I had a lapse in coverage. But I didn't! I had the confirmation email right there in my inbox, dated the exact day my policy renewed. I had to sit on hold for forty-five minutes listening to this terrible, staticky elevator music. It sounded like someone playing a keyboard underwater. And when I finally got a real person on the line, he tried to tell me it was a system glitch related to the leap year. A leap year glitch! In this day and age, how does a massive financial institution not have their databases properly coded to handle a calendar anomaly that happens every four years? It's just lazy programming, honestly. If I made a calculation error like that on a bridge truss, people would literally die. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, the divorce. Yeah, the depression really just clamped down on me about a month ago when all the money stuff got finalized.
Aside from the heavy, hopeless feeling you described, have you lost interest or pleasure in the hobbies or activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... hobbies? I don't... I mean, I guess I used to like doing things, but lately, no, not really. I just don't have the energy for anything. 

I used to really love doing these intricate jigsaw puzzles, you know? The ones with like, three thousand pieces that take up the entire dining room table. I had this one of the Neuschwanstein Castle in Germany that was just beautiful. But you know what's crazy about castles? The structural integrity of those old stone walls is actually fascinating when you think about the mortar they used back then. They didn't have Portland cement, obviously, so they used this lime-based mixture that actually heals its own micro-cracks over time when it gets wet. It's brilliant, really. We spend millions developing these high-tech self-healing concrete polymers now, and they were basically doing a primitive version of it centuries ago. 

Actually, that reminds me of this contractor I had to deal with on a site inspection last month. He was trying to cut corners on the rebar spacing for a retaining wall, and I had to just stand there and explain basic load distribution to him like he was a child. He kept saying, "Oh, it's close enough, sweetheart," and I just about lost my mind. Close enough? Gravity doesn't care about "close enough"! 

But um... wait, hobbies. Right. Yeah, no, I haven't even looked at a puzzle in months. I just... I don't care about them right now. I don't really care about much of anything.
Have you noticed if you are moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, feeling like you are unable to sit still and need to be constantly moving?

Um... moving slowly? I don't know, maybe? I guess I just feel like I'm dragging myself through mud most days. Everything just feels so heavy. 

Mud is actually a huge problem on construction sites right now because of all that rain we got last week. You know, when the soil gets oversaturated, the shear strength just completely plummets. We had this one site over on the east side where the excavation crew didn't properly slope the trench walls, and the whole thing just sloughed in after a downpour. It was a complete mess. They had to bring in these massive vacuum trucks just to clear out the slurry before they could even think about laying the pipe. And the smell! It's like this gross, sulfurous, rotting vegetation smell that just clings to your high-vis vest forever. I tried washing my gear three times with that heavy-duty sports detergent, but I swear I can still smell it when it gets humid. 

Which reminds me, my washing machine has been making this awful grinding noise during the spin cycle. It sounds like someone threw a handful of gravel in with the laundry. I looked up the schematic online, and I'm pretty sure the main drum bearing is shot, which is ridiculous because the machine is only three years old. Planned obsolescence is just out of control these days. They engineer these things to fail right after the warranty expires so you have to buy a new one. It's so wasteful. 

But um... what were you asking? Moving slowly? Yeah, I don't know. I'm not really paying attention to how fast I'm moving. I'm just tired.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively guilty or feeling like you are worthless because of the situation you are in?

Um... guilty? Worthless? Yeah. Yeah, a lot. I just keep telling myself I'm a terrible engineer, a failed wife... just a complete burden to everyone. I just lie there and replay every single missed calculation or tense email in my head, like it's all just proof that I ruin everything I touch. 

Speaking of emails, the server at work has been an absolute nightmare lately. They migrated us to this new cloud-based system over the weekend, and they promised it would be seamless, but it's been anything but. Half my archived project files from 2021 are just gone. Poof. And when you try to search for a specific keyword in the inbox, it just spins and spins and then crashes the whole application. I submitted a ticket to IT three days ago, and all I got was this automated response saying they're experiencing "higher than normal volume." Well, obviously! You broke the system! 

And the guy who runs IT, Greg... he always wears these really loud, patterned ties. Like, yesterday he had one with little cartoon golf clubs all over it. Who wears a golf tie to an office on a Tuesday? It just seems so unprofessional. It makes me think of my uncle, who used to wear these awful novelty socks to family dinners. He had this one pair that looked like sandals with socks underneath, which is just a visual paradox if you think about it. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Guilt? Right. Yeah, I just... I feel like everything falling apart is my fault. I just feel so useless.
